# Lab methods for DNA damage inside a lesion versus skin 5 mm away: outside AI report (unverified)

- **Origin:** an outside AI deep-research tool (Google Gemini), prompt 12 ("lab methods for DNA damage inside vs outside a spot": mtDNA deletions, telomere length, somatic mutations in single melanocytes or small clones), pasted by Ben into the project thread "Check DNA damage methods report" on 2026-11-28 13:21 UTC.
- **Status:** unverified leads, not medical advice. Module 5 (damage and repair) material. Nothing on this page may enter `data/evidence.csv`. None of the cited papers studies IGH or any white spot.
- **Part A** is the report as received, unchanged. **Part B** is the check of every quoted sentence and every number against the cited source. **Part C** is the checking thread's own judgment.

---

# Part A: report as received

Published methods comparing sun-exposed versus sun-protected skin—or lesions versus adjacent skin—differ sharply in tissue requirements, cellular resolution, and susceptibility to field effects within a 5 mm radius. Wherever a specific figure was unavailable in the indexed text retrieved for a paper, it is explicitly marked not found.

(a) Mitochondrial DNA Deletions

1. SYBR Green Real-Time PCR of the 4977 bp Common Deletion in Cryostat-Separated Dermis (Quan et al., 2015)

⚬ Biopsy size needed: 4 mm diameter full-thickness punch biopsies, cryostat-sectioned to a 1 mm depth to remove the epidermis (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6).
  "Skin samples were 4 mm diameter sections of full thickness skin." (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6)
  "To assess mtDNA common deletion in the dermis, the epidermis was removed using cryostat to cut at a depth of 1 mm (Fig. 1a)." (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6)
⚬ Number of subjects used: 10 subjects (mean age 54 years; exact age range/SD not found) providing paired sun-exposed forearm and sun-protected underarm samples (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6).
  "forearm and sun-protected underarm, respectively (N = 10, mean age 54" (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6)
⚬ What was measured: Relative level of the 4977 bp mtDNA common deletion in purified dermal DNA via SYBR Green real-time PCR, with epidermal-dermal separation verified by keratin 14 mRNA (82-fold lower in dermis) and type I procollagen mRNA (152-fold higher in dermis) (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6).
  "mtDNA common deletion (4977 bp) is one of the best described mitochondrial" (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6)
  "Real-time RT-PCR was performed by SYBR green real-time PCR using a 7300" (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6)
  "Keratin 14 mRNA levels in the dermal fraction were reduced 82-fold relative to the epidermis, indicating minimal contamination from keratinocytes in the dermal fraction, most likely from deeper appendages such as hair follicles and sweat glands (Fig. 1b). In contrast, type I procollagen mRNA levels were 152-fold greater in the dermis relative to epidermis, indicating collagen-rich dermis (Fig. 1b)." (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6)
⚬ Size of the difference found: Average dermal 4977 bp common deletion level was 6.9-fold larger in sun-exposed photodamaged forearm dermis than in sun-protected underarm dermis (for chronological aging in sun-protected buttock dermis, aged dermis was 4.5-fold greater than young dermis). Exact p-values and absolute deletion percentages: not found (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6).
  "The average level of mtDNA common deletion in photodamaged skin dermis was 6.9-fold larger compared to sun-protected skin dermis." (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6)
  "The average level of mtDNA common deletion in aged dermis was 4.5-fold greater compared to young skin dermis." (DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6)
⚬ Limits: Cryostat slicing at 1 mm removes the interfollicular epidermis (so epidermal lesions are not assayed) while still leaving residual epidermal appendage contamination ("minimal contamination from keratinocytes in the dermal fraction, most likely from deeper appendages such as hair follicles and sweat glands", DOI: 10.1186/s12929-015-0167-6). Paired comparison was between distant body sites rather than a lesion and skin 5 mm away.

2. PCR Incidence Assay of the 4977 bp Common Deletion in Sun-Exposed Skin and Epidermal Tumors (Birch-Machin et al., 1998)

⚬ Biopsy size needed: not found (PMID: 9457910, DOI: 10.1046/j.1523-1747.1998.00099.x).
⚬ Number of subjects used: 100 sun-exposed skin samples in the quoted comparison; total unique donors and sun-protected sample count not found (PMID: 9457910, DOI: 10.1046/j.1523-1747.1998.00099.x).
  "There was a significant increase in the incidence of high levels (i.e., >1%) of the 4977 bp deleted mtDNA in sun-exposed sites (27%, 27 of 100) compared with" (PMID: 9457910, DOI: 10.1046/j.1523-1747.1998.00099.x)
⚬ What was measured: Incidence of high levels (greater than 1%) of the 4977 bp mtDNA deletion by PCR in sun-exposed skin, sun-protected skin, and epidermal tumors (PMID: 9457910, DOI: 10.1046/j.1523-1747.1998.00099.x).
⚬ Size of the difference found: 27% (27 of 100) of sun-exposed sites carried greater than 1% of the 4977 bp deletion; the exact sun-protected percentage and p-value were not found. In epidermal tumors, deletions were absent in the epidermal component (PMID: 9457910, DOI: 10.1046/j.1523-1747.1998.00099.x).
  "Deletions were not seen in the epidermal component of several epidermal tumors" (PMID: 9457910, DOI: 10.1046/j.1523-1747.1998.00099.x)
⚬ Limits: Dichotomized threshold (greater than 1% incidence) lacks continuous quantitative resolution. Crucially for a lesion-versus-adjacent design, clonal proliferation in epidermal lesions can dilute or lose mtDNA deletions—corroborated by Eshaghian et al. (2006), who tracked the 4977 bp deletion alongside 3,715 bp and 6,278 bp deletions and reported that mtDNA deletions "are typically absent in nonmelanoma skin cancers" (PMID: 16374452, DOI: 10.1038/sj.jid.5700088):
  "Some mtDNA deletions were detected from the skin of multiple individuals, including 3,715 and 6,278-base pair (bp) deletions, whose frequencies approached that of the previously well-characterized 4977-bp "common" deletion." (PMID: 16374452, DOI: 10.1038/sj.jid.5700088)

3. TaqMan Real-Time PCR of the 3895 bp UV-Associated mtDNA Deletion in Tumor vs. Matched Perilesional Skin (Harbottle & Birch-Machin, 2006)

⚬ Biopsy size needed: Physical dimensions in mm not found (surgical excisions of non-melanoma skin cancer and matched perilesional skin). Epidermis and dermis were separated with 0.25% dispase at 4°C overnight, and PCR used 200 ng genomic DNA in a 25 μl reaction (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178).
  "For all perilesional skin samples, epidermis and dermis were separated using 0.25% dispase at 4°C overnight (Durham et al, 2003) and DNA was extracted using a Qiagen, DNeasy tissue extraction kit." (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)
  "The PCR was carried out in a 25 μl reaction containing 200 ng genomic DNA" (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)
⚬ Number of subjects used: Matched tumor vs. perilesional cohort: 5 basal cell carcinoma (BCC) patients (age 55–89 years, mean 78 years) and 5 squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) patients (age 70–87 years, mean 78 years). Sun-exposure cohort of clinically normal perilesional skin: 30 epidermis and 30 dermis samples from usually sun-exposed sites (mean age 70.45 ± 2.161 years); sample count for occasionally sun-exposed sites not found (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178).
  "Tumour and matched perilesional skin samples were taken with informed consent from patients undergoing excision of a NMSC, namely basal cell carcinoma (BCC) (n=5, age range 55–89 years (yrs), mean 78 yrs) or a squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) (n=5, age range 70–87 yrs, mean 78 yrs)" (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)
  "For the sun exposure studies, clinically normal perilesional skin was taken from body sites which are 'usually' exposed to the sun when outdoors (such as scalp, face, neck and ears) (epidermis n=30, dermis n=30, mean age ±s.e.m.=70.45±2.161)" (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)
⚬ What was measured: Junction-specific TaqMan real-time PCR quantifying the 3895 bp deletion (FAM-labeled probe spanning the 527//4450 junction relative to a VIC-labeled internal standard probe annealing to both wild-type and deleted mtDNA), plus 35-cycle standard PCR with a 30 s extension (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178).
  "Primers ISF/ISR and IS Probe, anneals to both wild-type and deleted mtDNA. Detection of the 3895 bp deletion was performed with primers 3895F/3895R and 3895 Probe. The specific 3895 Probe only anneals to deleted mtDNA as it binds across the deletion junction." (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)
  "The PCR conditions were 94°C for 10 min, 35 cycles of 94°C for 30 s, 56°C for 30 s, 72°C for 30 s and a final extension of 7 min at 72°C." (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)
⚬ Size of the difference found:
  ⚬ Usually vs. occasionally sun-exposed perilesional skin: significantly higher in usually sun-exposed skin (P = 0.0009 for dermis; P = 0.008 for epidermis); exact fold-change/means not found.
  ⚬ Dermis vs. epidermis: significantly higher in dermis than epidermis in both occasionally (P = 0.0143) and usually sun-exposed skin (P = 0.0007).
  ⚬ Tumor vs. perilesional skin: detected in 3 of 5 BCC and 3 of 5 SCC tumor samples; observed levels reached up to 2% in sun-exposed skin and 7% in NMSC samples; exact paired tumor-vs.-perilesional p-value not found (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178).
  "In specific terms, the quantitative real-time PCR analysis showed a significantly higher level of the deletion in the usually sun-exposed samples when compared to the occasionally sun-exposed samples (P=0.0009 for dermis, P=0.008 for epidermis; two-tailed t-test)." (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)
  "showing that the level of the 3895 bp deletion is significantly higher in the dermis compared with the epidermis both in the occasionally sun-exposed samples (P = 0.0143) and in the usually sun-exposed skin. (P = 0.0007)." (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)
  "In the tumour samples the deletion was present in three of five of both BCC and SCC patients (although not the same patients)." (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)
  "The 3895 bp deletion levels observed in this study are up to 2% in the sun-exposed skin samples and 7% in the NMSC samples" (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)
⚬ Limits: Bulk DNA extraction averages across focal high- and low-damage cells, and epidermal vs. dermal compartments differ markedly so whole-punch extraction without dispase separation confounds tissue-layer composition (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178).
  "Therefore, it is more likely that the levels observed in skin represent an overall average and that individual cells and/or focal areas will have several fold higher and lower areas of damage throughout the sample." (PMID: 16721366, DOI: 10.1038/sj.bjc.6603178)

(Note on benign sun-damage lesions: Hafner et al., 2011 compared the 4977 bp common deletion in benign skin lesions including solar lentigo and seborrheic keratosis and reported "the amount of the common deletion is significantly different in benign skin lesions," but biopsy sizes, subject counts, and effect sizes were not found in the retrieved abstract; PMID: 21255095, DOI: 10.1111/j.1600-0625.2010.01209.x.)

(b) Telomere Length

1. Tissue-Section Quantitative Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (Q-FISH) (Ikeda et al., 2014; Bottoni et al., 2019)

⚬ Biopsy size needed: not found in retrieved text for either study (assayed on histological tissue sections from excised skin/actinic keratosis/SCC and surrounding or flanking skin; exact punch diameter or section thickness not found; PMID: 24411948, DOI: 10.1016/j.humpath.2013.10.009; DOI: 10.1038/s41467-019-11785-7).
⚬ Number of subjects used: not found in retrieved text (Bottoni et al., 2019 notes "multiple patients" without an exact retrieved count; DOI: 10.1038/s41467-019-11785-7).
⚬ What was measured:
  ⚬ Ikeda et al. (2014): In situ telomere length by Q-FISH in epidermis of skin with/without sun exposure, actinic keratosis, and epidermis surrounding actinic keratosis (PMID: 24411948, DOI: 10.1016/j.humpath.2013.10.009).
  ⚬ Bottoni et al. (2019): Q-FISH telomere fluorescence in stroma underlying actinic keratosis versus flanking unaffected skin, plus qPCR average telomere length normalized to ALBUMIN in matched dermal fibroblasts from SCC and flanking skin (DOI: 10.1038/s41467-019-11785-7).
  "AK underlying stroma versus flanking unaffected skin from multiple patients." (DOI: 10.1038/s41467-019-11785-7)
  "d qPCR analysis of average telomere length normalized to the ALBUMIN gene in HDFs" (DOI: 10.1038/s41467-019-11785-7)
⚬ Size of the difference found: Numerical telomere-to-centromere ratios (TCR), base-pair differences, and p-values: not found in retrieved text. Qualitatively, Ikeda et al. (2014) found shorter telomeres in sun-exposed skin and in histologically normal epidermis surrounding actinic keratosis (PMID: 24411948, DOI: 10.1016/j.humpath.2013.10.009).
  "Our findings demonstrate that sun exposure induces telomere shortening and that actinic keratosis arises from epidermis with shorter telomeres despite the absence of any histologic atypia." (PMID: 24411948, DOI: 10.1016/j.humpath.2013.10.009)
⚬ Limits:
  ⚬ Field effect 5 mm away: Because actinic keratosis arises from surrounding epidermis that already carries shortened telomeres without histologic atypia (Ikeda et al., 2014; PMID: 24411948), a 5 mm perilesional control may show little contrast against the lesion itself.
  ⚬ Assay variance: In a meta-analysis of telomere assays, Q-FISH showed a reported coefficient of variation of 12.4%, while qPCR CVs ranged from 0.37% to 28% across laboratories (Wentzensen et al., 2011; DOI: 10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-11-0005).
  "One publication which used Q-FISH reported a CV of 12.4% (38)." (DOI: 10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-11-0005)
  "Published coefficients of variation (CVs) for this method ranged from 0.37% to 28%. This wide range suggests substantial variability between laboratories." (DOI: 10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-11-0005)

2. Bulk Epidermal Telomere Length Assay (Sugimoto et al., 2006)

⚬ Biopsy size needed: not found (PMID: 16524700, DOI: 10.1016/j.jdermsci.2006.02.004).
⚬ Number of subjects used: not found (PMID: 16524700, DOI: 10.1016/j.jdermsci.2006.02.004).
⚬ What was measured: Telomere length in epidermis from sun-exposed versus sun-protected sites (specific molecular assay method not found in retrieved abstract; PMID: 16524700, DOI: 10.1016/j.jdermsci.2006.02.004).
⚬ Size of the difference found: No statistically significant difference between sun-exposed and sun-protected epidermis; exact kb values and p-value not found (PMID: 16524700, DOI: 10.1016/j.jdermsci.2006.02.004).
  "Unexpectedly, telomere length was not significantly different between epidermis from sun-exposed sites and from sun-protected sites. Conclusion: We could not show the evidence that telomere shortening is associated with photoaging of the skin." (PMID: 16524700, DOI: 10.1016/j.jdermsci.2006.02.004)
⚬ Limits: Bulk epidermal measurements mix basal and suprabasal layers and can be blunted by epidermal telomerase induction (Vandiver & Hogan, 2020; DOI: 10.20517/2347-9264.2020.159):
  "studies focused on the epidermis suggest telomerase may be expressed in basal keratinocytes and increase with sun exposure and inflammation[42-44], correlating with a low magnitude of telomere length decrease with age." (DOI: 10.20517/2347-9264.2020.159)

3. Luminex-Based Relative Telomere Length (RTL) Across Multi-Tissue GTEx Samples (Demanelis et al., 2020)

⚬ Biopsy size needed: not found (DOI: 10.1126/science.aaz6876).
⚬ Number of subjects used: 6,391 unique tissue samples across all GTEx tissue types; the specific sample count for the sun-exposed versus non-sun-exposed skin subset was not found in retrieved text (DOI: 10.1126/science.aaz6876).
  "RTL was measured for 6391 unique tissue samples using a Luminex assay, generating the largest publicly available multitissue TL dataset." (DOI: 10.1126/science.aaz6876)
⚬ What was measured: Relative telomere length (RTL) by Luminex hybridization assay across human tissues including sun-exposed skin ("skin–sun exposed", DOI: 10.1126/science.aaz6876).
⚬ Size of the difference found (sun-exposed vs. not-sun-exposed skin): not found in retrieved text (DOI: 10.1126/science.aaz6876).
⚬ Limits: Bulk tissue homogenate without cell-type resolution; specific technical limits for skin in the retrieved text: not found.

(c) Somatic Mutation Burden in Single Melanocytes or Small Clones

1. Single-Cell Clonal Expansion and Sequencing of Individual Melanocytes (Tang et al., 2020)

⚬ Biopsy size needed: Minimum total biopsy area not found; excised skin (stored at 4°C and processed in under 24 h) was trimmed of excess dermis and diced into pieces of approximately 2×2 mm² (4 mm²), digested in 10 mg/ml dispase II for 18 h at 4°C, epidermal-peeled, dissociated with 0.5% trypsin-EDTA at 37°C for 4 min, and cultured for 7–14 days (PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8).
  "Skin tissue was stored at 4°C and processed in under 24h from time of collection." (PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8)
  "Excess dermis was trimmed off and the remaining skin was cut into pieces (approximately 2x2 mm2) using surgical scalpel blades. Tissue was incubated in 10mg/ml dispase II (Thermo #17105-041) for 18hr at 4°C. The epidermis was peeled away from the dermis, incubated in 0.5% trypsin-EDTA (Thermo #15400-054) at 37°C for 4 min, and neutralized with 0.5mg/ml soybean trypsin inhibitor (Thermo #17075-029)." (PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8)
  "Cells were incubated at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 7–14 days." (PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8)
⚬ Number of subjects used: Exact total number of human donors not found in retrieved text. Individual melanocyte counts by sun-exposure class were n = 24 from chronically sun-exposed sites, n = 105 from intermittently sun-exposed sites, and n = 4 from sun-shielded sites (PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8).
  "b, Comparisons between mutation burden of chronically sun-exposed (n=24), intermittently sun-exposed (n=105), and sun-shielded sites (n=4)." (PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8)
⚬ What was measured: Somatic mutation burden (mutations/Mb), mutational signatures, and clonal phylogenetic relatedness across single melanocytes from chronically exposed, intermittently exposed, sun-shielded, and skin-cancer-adjacent normal skin (PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8).
  "We found shared mutations between nine separate pairs or trios of melanocytes, suggesting that these cells stem from clonal fields of melanocytes in the skin (Fig. 4 and Extended Data Fig. 7)." (PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8)
⚬ Size of the difference found: Melanocytes adjacent to a skin cancer carried higher somatic mutation burdens than melanocytes from donors without adjacent skin cancer; exact median/mean mutations/Mb values and ANOVA p-values were not found in retrieved text (PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8).
  "Melanocytes located adjacent to a skin cancer had higher mutation burdens than melanocytes from donors" (PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8)
⚬ Limits:
  ⚬ Requires fresh viable tissue (processed in under 24 h) and 7–14 days of ex vivo clonal expansion, which selects for proliferating cells and introduces tissue-culture mutations (exact rate not found because the leading digit was truncated in the retrieved snippet as "... 045 mutations/Mb per 7 days in tissue culture."; PMID: 33029006, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-020-2785-8).
  ⚬ Clonal fields of related melanocytes ("nine separate pairs or trios of melanocytes") exist in clinically normal skin, meaning paired samples 5 mm apart can share a common mutated precursor.

2. Gridded 2 mm² Epidermal Micro-Biopsy Ultra-Deep Targeted Sequencing (Fowler et al., 2021)

⚬ Biopsy size needed: Detached epidermal sheets cut into a gridded array of 2 mm² pieces, each containing approximately 10⁵ nucleated cells (about 3×10⁴ basal cells), with an average of 39 grids of 2 mm² sequenced per site (1,261 pieces totaling 25.2 cm² across all donors) (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092).
  "Sheets of epidermis were detached from the underlying dermis and cut into a gridded array of 2mm2 pieces, each containing approximately 105 nucleated cells of which ca. 3×104 were in the proliferative basal cell layer (4)." (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
  "A total of 1,261 2mm2 pieces were sequenced at an average coverage of 690x using a bait set of 74 cancer associated genes (Figure 1c, Table S2, Table S3) (1)." (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
  "In a total area of 25.2cm2 of skin sampled across all donors" (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
  "An average of 39 2mm2 grids were" (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
⚬ Number of subjects used: 35 Caucasian donors (ages 26–79) across 37 anatomical positions grouped into 5 body sites (abdomen, head, forearm, leg, trunk); skin-type data were available for 24 donors (19 with Fitzpatrick types 1 and 2), and occupational history for 28 donors (8 outdoor workers for 5 years or more; 6 indoor workers who lived in subtropical/tropical countries) (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092).
  "Normal skin from chronically and intermittently sun exposed sites was collected from 35 Caucasian donors whose ages ranged from 26-79 with a balance of males and females (Figure 1b, Table S1)." (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
  "A total of 35 patients were sequenced across 37 positions clustered into five main sites; abdomen, head, forearm, leg, and trunk." (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
  "Information on skin type was available for 24 donors, 19 of whom had pale skin, a history of severe sunburn and limited ability to tan (Fitzpatrick type 1 and 2) (Table S1). Eight of 28 donors with an occupational history had worked outside for 5 years or more, while of the indoor workers six had lived in subtropical or tropical countries." (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
⚬ What was measured: Somatic mutations in 74 cancer-associated genes at 690× mean sequencing depth using ShearwaterML (detecting variants in 1% or less of nucleated cells), yielding 47,977 single base substitutions (SBS), 3,824 double base substitutions (DBS), and 2,090 small (less than 200 bp) indels, plus copy number alterations (found in 10% of clones on fine-scale mapping) and hair-follicle comparisons (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092).
  "Mutations were called using the ShearwaterML algorithm which detects mutations present in 1% or less of nucleated cells in the sample (5,6)." (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
  "we identified 47,977 single base substitutions (SBS), 3,824 double base substitutions (DBS) and 2,090 small (<200 bp) insertion or deletion events (indels) after merging mutations shared between adjacent samples" (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
  "Fine scale mapping revealed 10% of clones had copy number alterations. Analysis of hair follicles showed mutations in the upper follicle resembled adjacent skin, but the lower follicle was sparsely mutated." (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
⚬ Size of the difference found: Raw site totals included 14,561 mutations in the head versus 10,515 mutations in the trunk; normalized mutations/Mb per site and statistical p-values for head versus trunk/leg/abdomen/forearm were not found in retrieved text (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092).
  "Head = 14561 mutations, Trunk = 10515 mutations." (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
⚬ Limits:
  ⚬ Millimeter-scale heterogeneity: A single 2 mm² sample 5 mm away can land in a completely different clonal patch (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092):
    "Clonal burden, mutational processes and competitive selection varied both across body sites and within millimeters in individual skin samples." (DOI: 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-20-1092)
  ⚬ Cell-type and clone-size floor: Bulk 2 mm² epidermal sequencing (~10⁵ cells, ~1% variant allele frequency floor) primarily captures keratinocyte clones and misses isolated single melanocytes; hair-follicle inclusion also dilutes mutation counts because the lower follicle is sparsely mutated.
  ⚬ Targeted panel & cohort scope: Captures only 74 positively selected cancer genes rather than genome-wide neutral mutation burden, and all 35 donors were Caucasian.

Methodological Comparison for a Paired Lesion vs. 5 mm Adjacent Design

Target	Representative Method	Biopsy Size Needed	Subjects / Samples	Key Design Risk at 5 mm Spacing
(a) mtDNA deletions	SYBR Green qPCR (4977 bp, Quan et al., 2015) / TaqMan qPCR (3895 bp, Harbottle & Birch-Machin, 2006)	4 mm punch (1 mm cryostat cut) / 200 ng DNA from dispase-separated skin	N = 10 paired / n=5 BCC, n=5 SCC, n=30 usually exposed	Epidermis vs. dermis differ (P = 0.0007–0.0143); proliferating lesions can lose deletions relative to adjacent photoaged skin
(b) Telomere length	Tissue-section Q-FISH (Ikeda et al., 2014; Bottoni et al., 2019) / Bulk assay (Sugimoto et al., 2006) / Luminex (Demanelis et al., 2020)	not found	not found (skin cohorts); 6391 GTEx multi-tissue samples	Histologically normal skin adjacent to AK already has short telomeres (field effect); bulk epidermis shows no sun-exposure difference
(c) Somatic mutations	Single-melanocyte culture + sequencing (Tang et al., 2020) / Gridded 2 mm² 690× targeted sequencing (Fowler et al., 2021)	2×2 mm² diced fresh pieces (under 24 h) / 2 mm² epidermal grids	n=24 / n=105 / n=4 melanocytes / 35 donors (1,261 grids)	Clonal burden varies within millimeters; clonal melanocyte fields can span both lesion and 5 mm control; culture adds mutations

Designing a paired intra-individual comparison between a small sun-damage lesion and skin 5 mm away requires guarding against three recurring confounders across these assays: compartment mixing (separating epidermis from dermis via dispase or cryostat sectioning, or using spatially resolved Q-FISH, because dermal and epidermal mtDNA deletion burdens and telomere dynamics diverge), field effects at 5 mm (both telomere shortening around actinic keratosis and mutant clonal fields extend into histologically normal perilesional skin, so adding a distant sun-protected intra-individual control helps distinguish lesion-specific signal from local field damage), and biopsy-splitting trade-offs (fresh viable tissue is mandatory if culturing single melanocytes, whereas FFPE/frozen sections serve Q-FISH and micro-biopsy DNA serves mtDNA qPCR and ultra-deep targeted sequencing).

Every quoted sentence was matched by script against the saved source text (case, spacing, dashes and curly quotes normalised; nothing else). Every number in the report's prose was then looked up by hand. Source texts are in the project files folder `papers/excerpts/` and are not committed.

## B2. Quoted sentences: 55 checked

- **53 found word for word.**
- **1 found with a small change:** Vandiver & Hogan: the source ends "...decrease with age[43]."; the report drops the citation marker "[43]". The meaning is unchanged.
- **1 misread:** Tang 2020, "... 045 mutations/Mb per 7 days in tissue culture." The report says a leading digit was cut off, so the rate was "not found". The source prints the rate as ".045" (0.045), in full: "we estimate that mutations occur at a rate of .045 mutations/Mb per 7 days in tissue culture." The paper then says "we conclude that the number of mutations accumulated in tissue culture was negligent" (sic; read as negligible). So the report's limit "introduces tissue-culture mutations" is the reverse of the authors' conclusion.
- **2 verbatim but put in the wrong context (Bottoni 2019):** see B3.

It is a DNA-break stain, not a telomere measurement. Q-FISH in this paper is done on cultured fibroblasts: "Telomeric DNA Q-FISH ... in HDFs plus/minus CSL silencing". | DOES NOT MATCH |

No exposed-versus-unexposed difference was found in the saved text, so "not found" stands for the difference. | Partly available |

## B4. Numbers in the report's prose that do match

Quan 2015: 4 mm samples, 1 mm cryostat cut, N = 10, 82-fold, 152-fold, 6.9-fold, 4.5-fold (aged group from sun-protected buttock skin, N = 8 young and N = 8 aged). Harbottle 2006: 0.25% dispase, 200 ng DNA in 25 μl, BCC n = 5 and SCC n = 5 with the ages given, n = 30 usually exposed, P = 0.0009, 0.008, 0.0143, 0.0007, three of five tumours, up to 2% and 7%, the 527//4450 junction, FAM and VIC reporters, 35 cycles and a 30 s extension. Birch-Machin 1998: 27% (27 of 100). Wentzensen 2011: 12.4% and 0.37% to 28%. Demanelis 2020: 6391 samples. Tang 2020: under 24 h, about 2×2 mm², 10 mg/ml dispase for 18 h, 0.5% trypsin for 4 min, 7 to 14 days, n = 24 / 105 / 4 melanocytes, nine pairs or trios. Fowler 2021: about 10^5 cells and 3×10^4 basal cells per 2 mm² piece, 1,261 pieces, 690x, 74 genes, 25.2 cm², 35 donors aged 26 to 79, 37 positions, 5 sites, 24 / 19 and 8 of 28 / 6, 1% detection floor, 47,977 / 3,824 / 2,090 mutations, 10% of clones, 14,561 and 10,515.

## B5. Statements that are the report's own reasoning, not quoted

These have no source sentence behind them and are leads only: that Quan's cryostat cut "removes the interfollicular epidermis (so epidermal lesions are not assayed)"; that "clonal proliferation in epidermal lesions can dilute or lose mtDNA deletions" (Eshaghian's abstract says only "implying a potential selection for full-length mtDNA or perhaps a protective role"); that bulk epidermis "mix[es] basal and suprabasal layers" (Vandiver & Hogan do not say this); that a 2 mm² grid "misses isolated single melanocytes"; that Fowler's 74 genes are "positively selected"; and the whole closing paragraph on three confounders.

---

# Part C: the checking thread's judgment (not evidence)

- **Reliable for planning:** the method details for Quan 2015, Harbottle 2006, Tang 2020 and Fowler 2021, and the CV figures from Wentzensen 2011. The quotes are real and the numbers match.
- **Do not rely on:** the Bottoni 2019 rows (no tissue telomere measurement in AK or SCC versus flanking skin exists in that paper; the quoted lines are a DNA-break stain and a cultured-cell knockdown); the claim that tissue culture adds meaningful mutations in Tang 2020 (the authors measured 0.045 per Mb per week and called it "negligent", read as negligible); every "not found" for subject counts, because 8 of them were printed in the source.
- **More useful than the report makes it look:** Hafner 2011 is the only cited study that compares a benign sun-damage lesion directly with adjacent normal skin, and its abstract shows the lesion can sit either above or below the adjacent skin depending on lesion type (lower in all 8 SK, higher in half of 14 SL). For an IGH design this argues for measuring both directions, not assuming the spot is worse. The full text is paywalled.
- **Still true after the check:** none of these papers looks at IGH or any white spot. The design risks the report names (separating epidermis from dermis, field effects close to a lesion, and a distant sun-protected control in the same person) are each supported by at least one quoted source: Harbottle's dermis-versus-epidermis P values, Ikeda's shorter telomeres in the epidermis around actinic keratosis, Fowler's variation "within millimeters", and Tang's clonal fields.
- Nothing here enters the ledger. Extracting any of these papers needs Ben's separate yes.
